findings.issue: decideBot(view, style, seed = 0) silently gives a fixed seed when a caller leaves it out. The worker then accepts 0 as valid. Today's only caller (useTableSession.requestBotDecision) passes turn.seed, so there is no reachable path. It is a fail-open default that could hide a future caller that forgets the seed, and all of that caller's bot draws would come from one constant stream.
findings.evidence: No reachable path: grep shows one caller, src/ui/table/useTableSession.ts:51, and it passes turn.seed.
findings.fix: Optional: make `seed` a required parameter so the compiler catches a missing seed.

summary: No BLOCKER, MAJOR or MINOR findings. Hidden information (REQ-025): the worker payload is {id, kind, view, style, seed}. view is playerView(hand, seat), the bot's own view as before. The replay code stays on the main thread: it appears only in session.ts botTurn, and nothing in src/ui sends it. The seed can't be traced back to the deck. shuffledDeck seeds its xoshiro state from all 128 bits of the replay code through the bijective mixState128. The bot seed is the (k+1)-th xoshiro output from Xoshiro128(fnv1a32(`${code}/${seat}`)). Every seat shares one 32-bit FNV prefix state over the code, so even an observer who sees every seed and brute-forces 2^32 values learns at most about 32 bits of a 128-bit secret. That leaves about 2^96 candidate codes and nothing usable about the deck. The worker also has no other input it could combine with the seed. The replay code itself still comes from crypto.getRandomValues. A non-cryptographic PRNG for bot mixing fits the spec (the goal is reproducibility, not unpredictability). Worker input handling: handleAdviceRequest checks the message shape, then isSeed checks that the seed is a number, an integer and in 0..0xffffffff before botRandom, which checks again. Bad input becomes an ok:false TypeError. This fails closed, the error message doesn't echo the value, and an attacker gets nothing extra (the only sender is the same-origin main thread). The new lint rule (Math.random/Date/crypto/performance in src/bots and src/advice) only adds restrictions. No new dependencies, secrets, injection sinks or unbounded loops: botDecisionSeed loops once per earlier action by the seat, which the betting rules bound. semgrep isn't installed, so no scanner was run.
